title: Tenant geo-guards: retention enforcement and automated compliance exports for Dedicated
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Enterprise customers using Redwood Dedicated require verifiable controls showing that tenant data is stored in the requested geography, retained only per contract, and that evidence (attestations, manifests, and logs) can be exported to auditors. Current Dedicated deployments track region metadata, but retention enforcement is partially manual and evidence packaging is ad-hoc.

Goal: Implement per-tenant retention enforcement (policy->enforcement chain), a tamper-evident evidence export pipeline that generates signed artifacts for audits, and UX/API surfaces for scheduled and on-demand compliance report generation. The feature set will be called 'Tenant Geo-Guards' and should support monthly automated attestations and on-demand exports for customers with Dedicated contracts.

Scope:
- Per-tenant metadata mapping: canonical storage location labels (region, availability zone, storage class) stored in tenant config.
- Retention enforcement: lifecycle rules applied to tenant datasets and KV caches with automated deletion/expiration and audit markers.
- Evidence export pipeline: collate manifests, retention policy evaluations, access logs, KMS audit entries, and produce a signed bundle (JSON manifest + checksums + signature).
- Automation: scheduled generation (monthly) + on-demand via Console/API.
- Console: add a Compliance > Residency & Retention page with last attestations, retention timeline, and download link for export bundles.
- API: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/compliance/export to trigger on-demand exports and GET to list previous exports.
- Security: sign bundles with HSM-backed keys and include certificate chain.

Out of scope: cross-tenant live data movement tooling, full legal attestations (legal will review generated artifacts).
acceptance_criteria:
- Each Dedicated tenant has a canonical 'data_residency' metadata field visible in tenant config and Console.
- Retention policies (per-tenant) can be set via API and Console and are enforced by automated lifecycle jobs with observable metrics.
- Monthly automated attestation bundles are produced for tenants flagged for compliance, stored in an immutable audit bucket, and available for download for 90 days.
- Generated bundles include: metadata manifest, per-bucket/object checksums, retention evaluation log, access log slice for the period, and a signature created with Redwood KMS-HSM.
- Console shows last attestations and a download button; API endpoints exist for programmatic retrieval.
- E2E test covering creation of policy, simulated writes, retention expiry, bundle generation, and signature verification.
- Security review completed and incident playbook for false positives documented.
- Performance: attestation generation for a medium tenant (<5M objects) completes within 20 minutes; pipeline scales horizontally.
implementation_notes:
Architecture plan:
1) Tenant metadata store: extend tenant-service to persist explicit residency metadata and retention policy id.
2) Retention enforcement: implement retention-evaluator service that reconciles policies to storage lifecycle rules (S3 lifecycle / object TTLs) and issues delete/expire operations. Use existing autoscaler patterns for batch reconciliation.
3) Evidence pipeline: build compliance-export service that orchestrates: (a) manifest collector (object list + checksums), (b) retention-eval snapshot, (c) access log slicer (from logging pipeline), (d) KMS signing step that uses HSM-wrapped keys per-region. Output: signed ZIP with manifest.json, checksums.csv, retention_report.md, access_logs_slice.json, signature.sig.
4) Storage: write bundles to immutable audit-bucket with server-side encryption and retention lock; generate pre-signed download links for Console and API.
5) Console/UI: Compliance page with scheduled job configuration and export history; reuse existing Logs/Downloads components.
6) API: define /tenants/{id}/compliance/export POST and GET endpoints; upstream rate limit and RBAC check.
7) Monitoring: metrics for exports_started, exports_failed, export_duration_seconds, retention_reconcile_errors. Add SLOs and alerting rules.
8) Tests: unit for policy mapping, integration test to run full pipeline against test bucket and verify signature.

Key implementation trade-offs:
- Tight coupling to cloud provider storage lifecycle vs custom garbage collection: choose lifecycle rules where available (faster, cheaper) and fall back to GC for on-prem.
- Bundle size vs atomicity: store full manifest and allow streaming downloads to avoid memory spikes.

Data privacy note: ensure export bundles redact PII unless explicitly requested; default bundle includes metadata and checksums only.
comments: 2025-11-05 - Triage: flagged as high priority for multiple enterprise deals; agreed to split into enforcement + export phases.
2025-12-01 - Architecture sync: decided to use provider lifecycle where available; retention-evaluator will have a provider adapter interface.
2026-01-18 - Security review (initial): SEC requested HSM-backed signing and per-region key material; ticket SEC-214 opened for key management changes.
2026-02-10 - Engineering design review: Luca to prototype manifest collector. Blocked temporarily by missing reader access to access-log index; infra to provide ACL (ticket INFRA-990).
2026-03-03 - First prototype: compliance-export service can generate small bundles and sign with test keys; PR link in links list. QA tests in progress.
